facts.claim: Term check, 26 November 2026: the AGD 'Get married' page (re-read in full) does not use the words 'marriage licence'. The only 'licence' on the page is 'identity (driver's licence or passport)'. The Australian step it describes is giving a notice of intended marriage form to an authorised marriage celebrant. None of the Australian government facts reused in this pack (AGD, Federal Register of Legislation, NSW, Victorian and Queensland registries, Services Australia, Smartraveller) use the term 'marriage licence' in the text recorded. This is a record of what was read, not a claim that no Australian source anywhere uses the term. The term 'marriage licence' / 'license' is used by the New Zealand Government (govt.nz) and the Hawaii State Department of Health.
facts.notes: Live re-check for marriage-licence stage 03, 26 November 2026 (apify web-fetch, HTTP 200).

facts.claim: As at November 2026, the Attorney-General's Department 'Get married' page (read live 13 November 2026; page metadata updated 13 June 2024): changes to the Marriage Act that became law on 12 June 2024: the option to have the NOIM witnessed remotely, via audio-visual link, as well as in person; an authorised celebrant must meet separately and in person with each party before the marriage is solemnised; re-ordering of the acceptable evidence of date and place of birth; clarifying that a NOIM can be transferred to another authorised celebrant, including at the request of the couple; clarifying that a celebrant must be physically present to solemnise a marriage, with the parties and 2 witnesses.
facts.notes: Copied from notice-of-intended-marriage 03-source-pack fact_07 (same claim, source, source_type and checked date).

facts.claim: The Attorney-General's Department's Notice of Intended Marriage publication page (last updated 22 December 2022) says section 42 of the Marriage Act 1961 requires that a marriage shall not be solemnised unless a notice in writing of the intended marriage (this form) is given to the authorised celebrant solemnising the marriage. The form is downloadable as PDF and DOCX.
facts.notes: Copied from notice-of-intended-marriage 03-source-pack fact_100 (same claim, source, source_type and checked date). Prior note: Orchestrator's live read, 13 November 2026 (early top-up).

facts.claim: AGD: the requirements for authorised witnesses remain unchanged and location-dependent. If the couple is in Australia, the person remotely witnessing the NOIM (which can include an authorised celebrant) must also be in Australia. If the couple is outside Australia, the authorised witness (which cannot be a celebrant) must also be outside Australia. A NOIM for a person or couple outside Australia cannot be witnessed online.
facts.notes: Copied from notice-of-intended-marriage 03-source-pack fact_102 (same claim, source, source_type and checked date). Prior note: Orchestrator's live read, 13 November 2026 (early top-up).

facts.claim: The Attorney-General's Department's list of prescribed authorities says a prescribed authority is an officer or employee of the Commonwealth, a State or Territory appointed by the Attorney-General, and is authorised, among other things, to authorise a marriage celebrant to proceed with a marriage ceremony where the minimum one-month notice has not been provided (shortening of time). The list is searchable by state and territory and includes registrars and deputy registrars of local courts and state registries of births, deaths and marriages.
facts.notes: Copied from notice-of-intended-marriage 03-source-pack fact_104 (same claim, source, source_type and checked date). Prior note: Orchestrator's live read, 13 November 2026 (early top-up).

facts.claim: Marriage Act 1961 (Federal Register of Legislation, latest compilation dated 28 March 2026, read live 13 November 2026; table of contents only, section text not returned): Part IV Division 2 includes s 41 'Marriages to be solemnised by authorised celebrant', s 42 'Notice to be given and declaration made', s 42A 'Commissioner of Australian Federal Police or approved authority may issue special notice', s 42B 'Authorised celebrant must physically meet each party to intended marriage separately', s 44 'Witnesses', and s 104 'Giving defective notice etc.' (offence). The Act is administered by the Attorney-General's Department.
facts.notes: Copied from notice-of-intended-marriage 03-source-pack fact_15 (same claim, source, source_type and checked date).

facts.claim: Before getting married you must apply for a marriage licence, which confirms it is legal for you to marry; a fee applies.
facts.notes: Copied from get-married-in-new-zealand 03-source-pack fact_201 (same claim, source, source_type and checked date).

facts.claim: You do not need to be a New Zealand citizen; visitors to New Zealand can marry in New Zealand.
facts.notes: Copied from get-married-in-new-zealand 03-source-pack fact_200 (same claim, source, source_type and checked date).

facts.claim: You need to arrange the licence at least 3 working days before you marry, and it expires after 3 months.
facts.notes: Copied from get-married-in-new-zealand 03-source-pack fact_202 (same claim, source, source_type and checked date).

facts.claim: Anyone can apply for a marriage licence online, whether in New Zealand or not; a paper form is also available.
facts.notes: Copied from get-married-in-new-zealand 03-source-pack fact_203 (same claim, source, source_type and checked date).

facts.claim: Couples outside New Zealand use the notice of intended marriage form for parties ordinarily resident outside New Zealand (BDM 58): fill it in except the statutory declaration, sign the declaration in front of an authorised person listed on the form, and send the fee to Births, Deaths and Marriages.
facts.notes: Copied from get-married-in-new-zealand 03-source-pack fact_205 (same claim, source, source_type and checked date).

facts.claim: When couples from outside New Zealand arrive in New Zealand, they need to visit a registry office to sign a declaration before the ceremony; addresses are on the application form.
facts.notes: Copied from get-married-in-new-zealand 03-source-pack fact_206 (same claim, source, source_type and checked date).

facts.claim: Signing the declaration is not the wedding ceremony; you declare you are legally allowed to marry and have been truthful on the form.
facts.notes: Copied from get-married-in-new-zealand 03-source-pack fact_207 (same claim, source, source_type and checked date).

facts.claim: For a personalised ceremony the couple is sent the licence and 2 copies of the Copy of Particulars of Marriage, and gives all 3 documents to the celebrant before the wedding.
facts.notes: Copied from get-married-in-new-zealand 03-source-pack fact_209 (same claim, source, source_type and checked date).

facts.claim: You can only have the ceremony in the places you put on the licence application, so include a back-up venue.
facts.notes: Copied from get-married-in-new-zealand 03-source-pack fact_210 (same claim, source, source_type and checked date).

insider_details.detail: Treat the NOIM as Australia's version of the licence step: it must reach your celebrant at least 1 month and no more than 18 months out, so for a wedding in Australia lodge it once the date and celebrant are locked, not in the last month. Shortening of time needs a prescribed authority's approval.

Couples living abroad can complete the NOIM overseas, but it cannot be witnessed online from outside Australia and the authorised witness there cannot be a celebrant, so book an authorised witness for the signing early.

The pretty certificate signed on the day is ceremonial. For a name change you need the official certificate from the state or territory registry, which the celebrant can order for you after they lodge the paperwork within 14 days.

Licence timing differs sharply overseas: New Zealand needs the licence at least 3 working days before and it lasts 3 months, with overseas couples signing a declaration at a registry office on arrival; Hawaii issues it in person no sooner than 30 days out and it lapses after 30 days. Build the arrival day and appointment into the itinerary.
In New Zealand you can only marry at the places named on the licence application, so name your back-up wet-weather venue on the application.

An overseas marriage cannot be registered in Australia, and some states won't accept the foreign certificate for a name change, so anyone planning to take their partner's surname after a wedding abroad should expect a separate change-of-name step at home.
